podcast.title: Initial Producer for *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got* (1990)
podcast.body: Nellee Hooper was initially hired to produce Sinead O'Connor's second album, *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got*. However, Sinead walked out after just two days, stating that they "couldn't get on together," leading to Chris Birkett taking over production. "Basically, the story is that they started off this album with another producer, Nelly Hooper. And the Shanade walked out after two days, they couldn't get on together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Member of The Wild Bunch
podcast.body: Nellee Hooper was a member of The Wild Bunch in Bristol during the 1980s. "A dentro de ahí teníamos también a Neil Hoper."

srcs.episode: Massive Attack y El Origen del Trip Hop en Bristol.

podcast.title: Influential British Producer
podcast.body: Nellee Hooper was one of the most important British music producers of the late 1990s, renowned for his work with artists like Björk, Madonna, and U2. He was also a member of the Wild Bunch movement in Bristol and collaborated with Björk on Trip Hop music which influenced Massive Attack. "Uno de los productores más importantes ya música británica de final de los 90."

podcast.title: Introduced Björk to Trip Hop and Electronic Sounds to U2 and Madonna
podcast.body: Hooper was instrumental in introducing Björk to the potent influences of Trip Hop, profoundly shaping her sound. He also introduced electronic sounds to U2 and worked on Madonna's more electronic productions towards the end of the 1990s. "pero sobre todo fue uno de los grandes productores de la época dorada de Bjork, que le introdujo en todas esas influencias tan potentes del trip home."

srcs.episode: Massive Attack y El Origen del Trip Hop en Bristol.

podcast.title: Prominent Producer in London
podcast.body: Later, in London, Nellee Hooper became a significant producer for various artists, including Madonna, U2 (initially referred to as "Doors" in the transcript, but clarified as U2 later), and Garbage. He was particularly renowned as one of the great producers during Björk's golden era. "Para el que no lo conozcáis Neil Hoper fue más adelante en Londres, productor de gente como Madonna, como Doors, como Garbage."

xref.title: Producer and Engineer for Sinead O'Connor (1990)
xref.body: Chris Birkett, who had previously mixed two singles from Sinead O'Connor's debut album, was contacted by Ensign Records executive Nigel Grainge to take over production for her second album, *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got*. This occurred after Sinead walked out on the original producer, Nellee Hooper. Birkett described the recording process as bare-bones and worked closely with Sinead, notably producing her hit single "Nothing Compares 2 U." "So the vocal company phoned me up, and signed records, Nigel Brange. And he said that we've got the studio booked, and Shanade's got all the songs ready. We don't have a producer. Could you mind taking it over?"
